component.name: tensorflow-serving
component.title: TensorFlow Serving
component.description: Run inference on the models of a TensorFlow Serving model server over gRPC, and get their status and metadata.
component.label: ai

configuration.description: The configuration that the endpoints start from. Each endpoint gets a copy of it, and the options of the endpoint replace its values.

modelName.label: common
modelName.description: The name of the model (servable) to call. The CamelTensorFlowServingModelName header replaces this option, and the model_spec of a request in the body replaces both. The option or the header must be set, even when the request in the body names the model.

modelVersion.label: common
modelVersion.description: The version number of the model to use. If no version and no version label is set, the server uses the best available version, typically the latest. The CamelTensorFlowServingModelVersion header replaces this option, and a version label, if one is set, is used instead of it.

modelVersionLabel.label: common
modelVersionLabel.description: The label of the model version to use, as assigned by version_labels in the model server configuration, for example stable or canary. The CamelTensorFlowServingModelVersionLabel header replaces this option. A version label is used instead of a version number.

signatureName.label: common
signatureName.description: The name of the signature (SignatureDef) of the model to evaluate, for classify, regress and predict. If not set, the server uses the default signature, serving_default. The CamelTensorFlowServingSignatureName header replaces this option.

target.label: common
target.description: The target of the gRPC channel to the model server, as host:port or as a gRPC target URI such as dns:///host:8500. The default is the gRPC port of TensorFlow Serving on the local host. The channel is created once, when the endpoint is initialized.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

credentials.label: security
credentials.description: The io.grpc.ChannelCredentials of the gRPC channel, for example a TlsChannelCredentials for TLS, given as a bean reference. If not set, InsecureChannelCredentials is used, and the calls are sent in plaintext.

CamelTensorFlowServingTarget.deprecationNote: Never read by the component. The gRPC channel is built once when the endpoint is initialised, so it cannot be redirected per exchange. Use the target endpoint option.
CamelTensorFlowServingTarget.description: The gRPC target of the model server. The component does not read this header. Deprecation note: Never read by the component. The gRPC channel is built once when the endpoint is initialised, so it cannot be redirected per exchange. Use the target endpoint option.

CamelTensorFlowServingCredentials.deprecationNote: Never read by the component. The gRPC channel is built once when the endpoint is initialised, so it cannot be re-authenticated per exchange. Use the credentials endpoint option.
CamelTensorFlowServingCredentials.description: The credentials of the gRPC channel. The component does not read this header. Deprecation note: Never read by the component. The gRPC channel is built once when the endpoint is initialised, so it cannot be re-authenticated per exchange. Use the credentials endpoint option.

CamelTensorFlowServingModelName.description: The name of the model (servable) to call. It replaces the modelName option, and the model_spec of a request in the body replaces it.

CamelTensorFlowServingModelVersion.description: The version number of the model to use. It replaces the modelVersion option. A version label, if one is set, is used instead of it.

CamelTensorFlowServingModelVersionLabel.description: The label of the model version to use, for example stable or canary. It replaces the modelVersionLabel option.

CamelTensorFlowServingSignatureName.description: The name of the signature (SignatureDef) of the model to evaluate. It replaces the signatureName option.

producerIn.description: The protobuf request of the api, or its Builder: a PredictRequest for predict, a ClassificationRequest or RegressionRequest, or the Input of one, for classify and regress. Another body that is not empty, such as text, JSON, bytes or a Map, is not parsed and fails the exchange with an InvalidPayloadException that names the request of the api: build the protobuf request before the endpoint. No body, a blank String or an empty byte array builds the request from the options and headers only, which is all model-status and model-metadata need; they read a GetModelStatusRequest or GetModelMetadataRequest when the body is one, and model-metadata asks for signature_def unless the request names its metadata fields. The model comes from the CamelTensorFlowServingModelName header, or else the modelName option

producerOut.description: The protobuf response of the api, such as a PredictResponse with the output tensors by name

api.description: The TensorFlow Serving API that the producer calls: model-status (GetModelStatus of the ModelService), or model-metadata (GetModelMetadata), classify, regress or predict of the PredictionService.
